title: Profinite limits are limits of underlying topological spaces
statement: Let $I$ be a small category and $F:I\to\mathsf{Profinite}$ a diagram of profinite spaces, meaning compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps. In compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention], let $(L,(p_i)_{i\in I})$ be a limit cone in $\mathsf{Profinite}$. The same cone is a limit in topological spaces. Explicitly, for every topological space $W$ and every compatible family of continuous maps $b_i:W\to F(i)$ there is a unique continuous map $b:W\to L$ such that $p_i b=b_i$ for every $i$. No compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $W$.
